clips.title: The story
paras: Gathering the Cure is an essential trial for young night elf druids learning to master nature's healing powers in Darkshore. Guided by Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine, the druid collects vital natural reagents to brew a restorative salve for the region's ailing wildlife. This task lays the practical foundation for understanding how herbal remedies combat venom and disease.

Following the discovery of a contaminated water source plaguing the local wildlife, Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine sets out to concoct an effective curative salve. While the sampled Cliffspring water forms the base of the mixture, genuine healing requires potent natural catalysts. The afflicted forest deer cannot recover on their own, making the gathering of wholesome remedies a matter of urgency for the Cenarion Circle.

The restorative salve demands two crucial flora: Earthroot and Lunar Fungus. Earthroot provides pure curative properties, requiring the practiced eye of an herbalist to harvest from the rocky soil. To lend the mixture potency, Alanndarian sends the druid into the nearby eastern caves to gather fungal blooms that flourish in the dark, nestled among increasingly territorial and agitated moonkin.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: The water will serve as the base of the curative salve I'll make for the deer. For curative properties, I need some earthroot. Herbalists know how to find it, so if we're unlucky and you aren't one then you'll need to find one to help us out.

Finally for potency, I need some lunar fungus. Finding lunar fungal blooms is easy enough; they're all over the place in caves just to the east of here. Moonkin reside in the caves and they're irritable as of late, so be careful.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Have you got the reagents I need to make the salve? The deer aren't getting any better on their own, so we better hurry to help them out!

clips.title: Completion
paras: This is good, friend, so much so that it should be enough to make some ample doses of the salve - at least enough to start to make a difference.

Making a cure for poisons can be quite difficult at times because each one often requires a very specific antidote to counteract it. Imagine being able to cure a poison at will without having to worry about the exact ingredients of what the antidote must be!
Now, let me get to work on this!
